title: Turing never called it that, and it didn't start with a machine at all
description:
Turing never called it that, and it didn't start with a machine at all His 1950 paper names it 'the imitation game': a man and a woman try to convince an interrogator, using written notes alone, which of them is which.

Convince the interrogator that he was the woman Turing's own sample question to the players was about hair length. Only after laying out that contest does he ask what happens if a machine takes the man's place, and whether it fools people just as often.

Published 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' in the journal Mind, opening not with a definition of thinking but with a parlour game about gender and deception.

He died in 1954. The name arrived afterwards, and without him.
